acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Every table in §3 names its owner contract (C1/C2/C3/C4/C7 or B1-4b) and its data class from §4; no orphan table.
AC-2: The audit-from-first-mutation mechanism is specified precisely enough that B1-2 can write a test proving a mutation without an audit row fails.

AC-3: No column or blob stores raw device output; the provenance record schema in §5 is complete (all fields of workflow §3.5) and states what the UI may and may not claim about discarded raw content.
AC-4: Per-component secret scopes are enumerated with storage, rotation and outage behaviour; no shared application secret exists.
AC-5: §8 lists every PostgreSQL-specific construct used and its Oracle equivalent or the reason none is needed.
AC-6: §9 gives at least eight testable acceptance criteria for the B1-2 Flyway V1 movement.
AC-7: §10 lists every contradiction with frozen authority found while writing (or states none were found and which documents were checked).
AC-8: The document introduces no decision that UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md reserves for the PO (RAW-RETENTION, DIRECTORY-POSTURE) -- those are referenced as decided/conditional, not re-decided.

baseline.sequencing: Runs concurrently with C2 (job execution contract, movement UI2_B0_C2_JOB_EXECUTION_CONTRACT). C1 owns the tables; C2 owns the job/lease/outcome semantics. Where C1 must name job tables, define only the columns C1 owns (identity, audit linkage, data class) and reference C2 for lifecycle columns by name -- do not duplicate C2's state machine. C3/C4/C5/C6/C7 come later and will reference this document.

context_not_loaded: Any Java source, Gradle build, Flyway migration file or Docker artefact -- B1 writes those against this contract
Line-1's utils/db_migrations.py and migrations/ as anything other than provenance: UI 2.0 does not share them (workflow P-1/P-4)
Device contact, credentials, network access of any kind
The identity/RBAC/session tables beyond the foreign keys C1 must reserve for them (C3 owns them)
invariants: Flyway is the ONLY migration authority for the UI 2.0 schema; no table is created or altered by application code, by Python, or by hand

RAW-RETENTION default NO: no column, table or blob stores raw device output; evidence rows carry a provenance record (run/step id, parser+capability version, capture/artefact id, source location, permitted sanitized fragment) per workflow §3.5

The audit table exists in migration V1 and every later mutation-bearing table is designed so that a mutation without an audit row is structurally impossible (state how: trigger, application-layer transaction rule, or both -- and which one is test-enforced)
Per-component secrets: the service, the worker, the scheduler and any adapter each have their own credential/secret scope; no shared 'app' secret; document storage, rotation and outage behaviour
Oracle portability rules from design §9 are preserved (no PostgreSQL-only types where a portable equivalent exists; name the exceptions)

Identifiers: device/cluster/context identities are opaque product identifiers; corporate hostnames/serials/IPs live only in fields the privacy law (PRIVACY_AND_DATA_HANDLING.md, DLP gate) classifies as such, never in log/audit free text
No decision already frozen in UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md is reopened; contradictions with any frozen authority are REPORTED in a dedicated section, never silently resolved

entries.subject: UI2 B0/C1 platform & schema contract -- complete, self-checked, merged
entries.text:
docs/design/UI2_0_C1_PLATFORM_SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md written (DRAFT -- FOR PRODUCT OWNER FREEZE), PR #163 merged (5ca75bf), follow-up bookkeeping PR #165 merged (69225ca). Self-check against the movement's AC-1..AC-8:

AC-1 (every table names owner + data class): satisfied -- section 3.1 ownership matrix covers all 9 tables (devices/endpoints/credential_references -> B1-4b; jobs/job_steps -> C1 identity + C2 lifecycle by reference; audit_log/provenance_records/secrets_metadata -> C1; cp_inventory_projection -> C1 + C4 by reference), each with an explicit data class from section 4. No orphan table.

AC-2 (audit-from-first-mutation mechanism precise enough for a B1-2 test): satisfied -- section 3.5 specifies a PostgreSQL AFTER-row trigger (fn_audit_capture, SECURITY DEFINER) requiring SET LOCAL app.actor_fingerprint/app.action_id in the same transaction; a mutation without that context raises audit_context_missing and never commits; ui2_app has no direct write grant on audit_log. Section 9 items 2-4 give the exact tests (bypass rejection, atomicity, trigger-coverage completeness).

AC-3 (no raw device output; provenance schema complete; UI claim rules stated): satisfied -- section 5's provenance_records table carries every field workflow section 3.5 names (run_id, step_id, parser_version, capability_version, capture_artifact_id, source_location, sanitized_fragment, fingerprint_sha256); section 5 states explicitly what the UI/API may and may not claim about discarded raw content.

AC-4 (per-component secrets, storage/rotation/outage, no shared secret): satisfied -- section 6.1 enumerates service/worker/scheduler/LDAP-adapter/migration-step scopes each with storage (DEV.2.1 <VAR>_FILE), rotation and fail-closed outage behaviour; no shared "app" secret anywhere.

AC-5 (every PostgreSQL-specific construct + Oracle equivalent or reason none needed): satisfied -- section 8's table covers GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, opaque TEXT ids, TIMESTAMPTZ, JSONB, the PL/pgSQL trigger, session GUCs and SECURITY DEFINER, each with its Oracle equivalent or a stated reason none is needed.

AC-6 (>= 8 testable B1-2 acceptance criteria): satisfied -- section 9 gives 10.

AC-7 (contradictions with FROZEN authority, or none + documents checked): satisfied -- section 10 states none found and lists every document checked; two documentation-hygiene gaps (a stale internal "S11.5" citation; PRIVACY_AND_DATA_HANDLING.md not yet naming UI 2.0's database) are flagged for the PO as open items, explicitly distinguished from contradictions.

AC-8 (no PO-reserved decision re-decided): satisfied -- section 7 references RAW-RETENTION (NO) and DIRECTORY-POSTURE (conditional) as already-decided/conditional throughout, never re-opened.

New finding id C1-1 minted for "audit from the first mutation" (section 1), correcting the stale "brief S11.5" citation propagated into UI2_0_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md:352 and this movement's own backlog note -- the brief has no S11 (it ends at S8); the actual correction is brief S8, quoted in full in section 1. Distinguished from SR-D8/DO-D8 (an unrelated key-custody finding, brief S4.1/K-7).

Validation: tests/test_architecture_convergence.py 22 passed. Full regression run in the foreground and awaited to completion (not backgrounded): 1829 passed, 63 failed, 148 errors -- every failure/error traced to this worktree's own missing/broken packages (cryptography not installed despite being in requirements.txt; paramiko broken, "'paramiko' is not a package"), confirmed pre-existing via git diff (only .md/.json changed) and identical tracebacks in unrelated modules never touched by this PR. Environment bootstrap was deliberately not attempted per AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md's no-bootstrap rule; reported, not fixed. Repository privacy gate: 5 pre-existing findings, confirmed byte-identical against origin/main outside this PR's diff hunks -- 0 new findings. git diff --check clean throughout.

A concurrent C2 dispatch (NXS-LOCAL-0052) and a VISUAL-DESIGN-LANGUAGE decision landed on origin/main mid-session, producing a real merge conflict in project/backlog.json (both sessions touched the same C1 backlog entry's note/target fields at dispatch time vs. completion time) -- resolved by keeping this movement's completion note as authoritative over the dispatch-time placeholder; project/roadmap.json and docs/design/UI2_0_BASELINE_CONTRACT.md merged cleanly. Full detail in project/build_history.json's ui2_b0_c1_platform_schema_contract record and the SESSION_CLOSE packet.
